summary: Segmented control is a row of two to five choices where exactly one is picked, shown as a raised knob that slides to it. Use it to switch between views of the same thing, like a calendar and a list, or to set one option from a few. It sits inline next to a title and changes what's below it at once. An option can be an icon alone, with its name as the label and a tooltip.
use: When people switch between a few views of the same content, like a calendar and a list of the same month.
When there are two to five short options and all of them should stay visible.
When the change should happen at once, without a separate Apply.
Not for more than five options, or long labels: use a select or tabs with an overflow then.
features: `options` are the choices, each with a `value` and a `label`. The picked one sits on a raised knob that slides and resizes to it. A `label` can be an icon alone: give the option a `title`, which names it for screen readers and shows as its tooltip.
`as="tabs"` (the default) makes it a tab list for switching a panel; `as="radio"` makes it a radio group for setting an option.
`id` ties the tabs to their panel: the panel takes `id="<id>-panel"` and `aria-labelledby="<id>-<value>"`.

The demo is a month of a pricing launch in one card. Its head is one line: October 2026 as the title between two quiet chevrons that step a month, and on the right the switch, two icons on the grey track, List and Calendar. The calendar is a calm month: a grey dot on each day with something on, the launch day's dot the one accent mark, today a quiet grey ring and the picked day a small accent circle, with the picked day's line under a hairline ("Oct 28 · Pricing goes live · 10:00"). Picking a day changes the line. The list shows the month's events as rows, a muted date, the event and its time on the right, with no lines between them and a quiet hover; a row opens its day in the calendar. Switching crossfades the two views, their days or rows coming in one after another, while the card eases to the new view's height; with reduced motion it switches at once. The demo goes from the calendar to the list and back on a calm loop, and stops for good once you click in it.
a11y: As tabs it is a `tablist` named by `label`, each option a `tab` with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`, and the panel a `tabpanel` labelled by the picked tab.
As a radio group it is a `radiogroup` with `radio` options and `aria-checked`.
Only the picked option is in the tab order. ← and → move and pick, wrapping at the ends, and Home and End jump to the first and last.
The knob is decoration; the picked option's state says the same.

In the demo, the switch's two icons are named List and Calendar, the chevrons Previous month and Next month, and each day in the calendar is a button named with its date and its event, with `aria-pressed` on the picked one; the picked day's line is a polite live region.

faq.q: Should it be tabs or a radio group?
faq.a: Tabs when it changes what a panel shows, like a calendar view. A radio group when it sets a value that's saved or sent, like a billing period.

faq.q: Can an option be only an icon?
faq.a: Yes. Put the icon in `label` and the option's name in `title`: the button takes it as its `aria-label` and shows it in a tooltip, as the demo's List and Calendar do.

faq.q: Does the knob slide when the labels change width?
faq.a: Yes. It measures the picked option whenever the control resizes, so it follows a translated label or a new font.

faq.q: How many options can it take?
faq.a: It works best with two to five short ones. Past that, the options get narrow on a phone.
